correctness.rationale: The underlying thin-spider distances imply exactly the stated P/M adjacency types. Each distinct leaf-label exchange needs two legal moves and endpoint parity supplies the extra pure-to-mixed move. Explicit legal M-mediated exchanges attain every lower bound, including the different-leaf mixed-to-mixed case, and clique changes with unchanged leaves cost one move. Cardinality, degree and edge counts follow by disjoint combinatorial counting, and the three-branch maximum gives the sharp diameter. A separate ground-up graph generator exhaustively verifies all 35 cases r=2..8, k=1..r and every pairwise distance; 20099 parameter comparisons check algebraic simplification. Finite checks do not replace the given universal proof.

value.rationale: The 2024 same-rule primary source explicitly poses the general shortest two-hop split-graph reconfiguration problem. The theorem gives a complete infinite natural subfamily classification: exact adjacency, an efficiently computable and constructive all-pairs geodesic metric, sharp three-regime diameter, and full vertex/edge/degree census. This is more than a routine reachability or small-parameter computation; it explains the Johnson-type geometry and the switch in the extremal regime as token density changes. It does not claim to solve the unrestricted problem.
